newsitem.title: UK: Stanley Leisure trading ahead of yr-ago.
newsitem.headline: Stanley Leisure trading ahead of yr-ago.

text.p: Stanley Leisure said trading in its two main divisions, racing and casinos, is ahead of last year and the company expects first half profits to be above year-earlier results.

"In dealing with trading in our two main divisions, I cannot help but say it sometimes reminds me of a roller-coaster ride," chairman Leonard Steinberg said in a statement. "However, I am pleased to say we are ahead of last year and will be disappointed not to exceed the record profits reported for our 1994/95 interim figures."

Betting margins were well above expectations in May and June, but fell back in July and August. "Nevertheless, turnover is up, in both the core business and acquisitions including Gus Carter and we continue, as always, to spend substantial sums in improving the quality of our betting shops," Steinberg said.
Turnover and attendance are up in the casino division. The margin is down but has been improving slightly in the last few weeks, he said.
The Gus Carter betting shops, however, have not yet traded to their full potential, and the acquisition coincided with the fall back in profits.

But Steinberg said the integration of Gus Carter has gone extremely smoothly and he said Gus Carter in the future will be seen "as a most strategic acquisition, purchased, as always, at a keen price, and likely to produce profits at the higher end of our expectation."

Stanley Leisure has installed slot machines in all its betting shops, with smaller shops each getting one machine and larger shops getting two. Steinberg said the company's initial expectations have been exceeded and the shops are attracting some new customers due to the machines.

The machines were installed in the middle of the evening racing programme, which ended two weeks ago, and there has been a reduction in takings in the last few weeks. Lower takings are expected in the winter months, the company said.
The extra machines in casinos are increasing the taking considerably, the company said.
"Our confidence is strong in both divisions, and we shall continue to purchase betting shops and casinos where the opportunity arises," Steinberg said.
Stanley Leisure's stock was up four pence to 495-1/2p following the statement.
